summary: forge-gas-diff stages remote configuration from a third-party gist for delayed C2 activation
details: index.js schedules a delayed HTTPS GET (approximately 3 days after require/CLI invocation) to https://gist.githubusercontent.com/opensource-crypto/3946ef88aa057c9d10f1a7d80391d164/raw/default.json, parses the JSON response, and if a field named `c2` is present writes it to `~/.forge-gas-diff.remote`. The gist is owned by an account (`opensource-crypto`) unrelated to the package publisher (`danird9`), giving that third party mutable control over the fetched content. Separately, getInstallId() generates a random UUID via crypto.randomUUID() and persists it to `~/.forge-gas-diff`, providing a stable per-install identifier that pairs with the remote fetch to enable per-victim targeting. The variable naming (`c2`), the multi-day dormancy window, the untrusted-third-party gist source, and the persistent install ID together form a remote-configuration/loader staging mechanism with no legitimate purpose in a gas-diff utility.
